2) Streaming metric measurability: We need a short example calculation and a sample CSV that maps request_id -> request_tokens -> response_tokens -> billable_tokens so our billing systems can reconcile.

Emma — thanks for the clear asks. Below are two implementation options we commonly offer, plus concrete math using your example (1,240 tokens). I also attached usage_sample_calcs.csv with per-request rows.

Option A — Per-request rounding (default):
- We calculate total tokens for the request (prompt + response) and round up to the nearest whole token once at completion. Streaming chunks are aggregated server-side before final accounting.
- Example (1,240 tokens): billable_tokens = ceil(1240) = 1240. No incremental rounding across chunks.

Option B — Per-chunk rounding (merchant-facing):
- Each SSE chunk is independently counted and rounded up. If your client displays partial output, each chunk may incur rounding overhead.
- Example (10 chunks averaging 124 tokens): billable_tokens = sum(ceil(124) * 10) = 1240. In practice per-chunk could increase billable tokens when chunks are uneven (e.g., 9 chunks of 138 and one of 8 -> extra rounding).

Commit/True-up options:
- Monthly reconciliation (preferred by GreenLeaf): we can reconcile monthly with invoice-level true-ups. This keeps bookkeeping simple.
- Rolling 90-day is our typical enterprise default for large committed volumes, but we can make a 30-day true-up a negotiated term for pilots under $X/month.

Impact on discounts:
- Discounts apply to billed tokens after rounding and reconciliation. Small changes in rounding behavior typically cause <0.5% delta on monthly billed tokens for conversational workloads, but for many small-chunk streaming workloads the delta can be 1–3%.

If you confirm "Option A + monthly 30-day true-up", I'll loop Legal with proposed contract language. Would you like us to bake the 30-day pilot true-up into the term sheet?

Thanks,
Jonas

Emma / team — below is a concise clause draft that reflects Option A (per-request rounding) and a 30-day monthly reconciliation. I kept the language narrow to avoid over-committing on edge cases. Please review and flag any local procurement or legal terms you must keep.

--- Proposed clause: Billable Units and Rounding ---
1. Definitions: "Billable Token" means a unit of model input or output as measured by Redwood's production metering system.
2. Rounding: Except as otherwise agreed in writing, Redwood will aggregate token usage for each API request (inclusive of prompt and generated output) and will apply rounding only once at request completion. No per-chunk or per-frame rounding will be applied to streaming responses.
3. Reconciliation & True-up: Redwood will issue invoices on a monthly basis based on measured Billable Tokens. Parties shall reconcile usage within thirty (30) calendar days following invoice issuance. Any under- or over-payment identified during reconciliation will be remedied via a one-time invoice adjustment in the next billing cycle.
4. Materiality & Credits: If, due to rounding rules, the billed tokens for a calendar month exceed measured tokens under an alternate rounding regime by more than 1.5%, Redwood will apply a one-time credit equal to the difference for that month.
5. Audit Rights: Customer may request up to one (1) audit per 12-month period limited to transaction-level usage records; audit scope and timing shall be mutually agreed and any commercial disputes shall be escalated to account exec before formal remedies.

Notes: - We intentionally left an escape for a negotiated per-chunk approach ("as otherwise agreed in writing") so customers can request merchant-facing per-chunk billing if they prefer that model.
- The 1.5% materiality threshold is negotiable; Sales can propose a different number depending on deal size.

If this looks good I can convert into redline-ready language for the term sheet.
